official_measurement_examples.name: Approved Document A scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document A covers structural loading and structural elements including foundations, walls, floors, roofs and chimneys.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2013 amendment date
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2013 Approved Document A and C amendments took effect from 1 October 2013.

official_measurement_examples.name: A3 robustness purpose
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government guidance on disproportionate collapse supports compliance with Requirement A3 and does not itself approve a specific design.

official_measurement_examples.name: Masonry technical note
official_measurement_examples.fact: The masonry disproportionate-collapse note is material-specific guidance and is not a universal structural design for every building.

official_measurement_examples.name: Car park research scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government car-park edge-protection reports are research and assessment guidance, not planning or building-control approvals for a site.

official_measurement_examples.name: Sulfate guidance scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Sulfate-damage guidance addresses diagnosis and remediation of affected concrete floors and does not prove a parcel is contaminated or structurally defective.

official_measurement_examples.name: Garden wall guidance
official_measurement_examples.fact: Garden-wall safety guidance provides inspection advice and indicative dimensions; it is not a planning permission or structural certificate.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part A structural compliance and town-planning permission are separate regulatory questions.

core_rules: Approved Document A compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not structural compliance
structural calculation is not building-control approval
building-control approval is not proof of as-built structural compliance
A3 robustness guidance is not a site-specific design certificate
disproportionate-collapse research is not a universal design rule
masonry guidance must not be applied to non-masonry systems without evidence
car-park edge-protection research is not a parcel planning constraint
garden-wall guidance is not a title-boundary determination
sulfate-damage guidance is not proof sulfate attack exists at a parcel
foundation design requires site-specific ground evidence
historic structural guidance must retain its edition and date
product or material evidence is not proof of correct installation
structural compliance does not create land or access rights
NO_DATA must remain NO_DATA rather than no structural constraint
no parcel structural clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
